feedback.problem: Let $F(x)=-4{x}^{2}-3x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **odd** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,\pi ),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,\pi ), \\ -F(-x), & x\in (-\pi ,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-\pi ,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-(-4(-x)^{2}-3(-x)) \\  & =-(-4{x}^{2}+3x) \\  & =4{x}^{2}-3x.\end{aligned}
$$
